Guess the run

The 2026 Chinook Run

Ganaraska and Credit counters: entries close Aug 31, 2026, 11:59 pm ET and model forecast frozen 19 Aug 2026

For past couple years I've been trying to predict the Chinook run. September numbers scribbled on the back of a datasheet and various modelling attempts. This fall I want to open it up and see how well my predictions hold up. I want to know whether it can beat your predictions, against the model's arithmetic, scored against the official season totals when the counters close.

The Details

Chinook die after spawning and come home almost entirely at ages 2–3, so every hatch year moves through as one countable wave. It takes the two-year-olds we counted last fall, scales them by how many age-3s have historically followed, and blends that with two honest baselines: last year's count, and the three-year average. A Monte Carlo simulation then replays the season 100,000 times with every ratio jittered within its own history to stress the assumptions, and the bands below are anchored to the model's real misses on past years. The full recipe, and everything the model watched along the way, is further down the page.

Click a level on each chart to cast your ballot, fine-tune it in the boxes, and submit. Closest combined call takes the prize: your choice of plushie from Freshwater Conservation Canada (there's a surprisingly accurate Chinook), with the purchase supporting freshwater projects across Canada.

How the Model Works

Three parts

1: A schedule

When They come home

Chinook spawn once and die, almost all at ages 2–4. Every hatch year moves through as one wave: jacks first, the bulk at age 3, stragglers at 4. Meet a wave early and you know what's still out in the lake.

2: A head count

We already met this year's fish

This fall's age-3 fish are last fall's age-2s. In 2025 the Ganaraska counted about 3,600 two-year-olds; history says roughly 1.5× as many age-3s follow, so ~5,400 of this run is already spoken for. Same arithmetic on the Credit at 1.8×.

3: An average

Three guesses, blended

The cohort math, "same as last year," and the three-year average each make a call; the headline is their average. Where they disagree is exactly how wide the error bands is real: the bands on the charts above come from the model's actual misses when re-forecasting past years, its typical miss for the dark band and double it for the light one.

The year-classes behind this forecast

In an average past year this method missed by about ±21% on the Ganaraska and ±45% on the Credit. That's the bar. Beat it and you've beaten the model.

Rules & Prize

Scoring

Your score is how far off you are on the Ganaraska plus how far off on the Credit, against the official published season total for each counter (the same series as the “last year” numbers on the ballot). Lowest total wins. Over or under doesn't matter; distance does.

Fine print

One ballot per person; resubmitting under the same name replaces it. Entries lock 11:59 pm ET, August 31, 2026. Ties go to the earlier ballot. The model competes, but its prize budget is zero.

The prize

Closest combined call collects: your choice of plushie from the Freshwater Conservation Canada shop. Bragging rights at the fishway included.
